content.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "In an era of rapid social development, it is vitally important to enhance young people's sense of responsibility." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
content.topic: Enhancing young people's sense of responsibility

modelEssay.title: Enhancing Young People's Sense of Responsibility
modelEssay.content:
In an era of rapid social development, it is vitally important to enhance young people's sense of responsibility. As technology advances and society transforms at an unprecedented pace, the younger generation is expected not only to keep up with change, but also to shoulder the duties that come with it.

On the one hand, a strong sense of responsibility drives personal growth. Young people who take their studies, work and commitments seriously tend to develop self-discipline and earn the trust of others. On the other hand, responsibility extends far beyond the individual. Whether it is protecting the environment, caring for family members, or contributing to the community, responsible youth become a powerful force for social progress. A volunteer who devotes weekends to helping the elderly, for instance, sets an example that inspires many others.

In conclusion, cultivating a sense of responsibility is essential for both self-fulfillment and the well-being of society. Therefore, families, schools and society as a whole should work together to help young people grow into responsible and reliable citizens of tomorrow.

structureAnalysis.paragraph1: 引入段：照抄题目给定句作为开头，点明社会快速发展的背景，提出年轻人需承担责任这一中心论点。
structureAnalysis.paragraph2: 展开段：从'促进个人成长'与'推动社会进步'两个层面论证责任感的重要性，并以志愿服务为例加以支撑。
structureAnalysis.paragraph3: 总结段：重申培养责任感对个人与社会的双重意义，呼吁家庭、学校与社会共同发力。

transcript.text: In America, at least, passion is a word that often comes up on job descriptions and in interviews.
transcript.translation: 至少在美国，'热情'是招聘说明和面试中经常出现的一个词。

transcript.text: On the whole, passionate people are thought of in a positive light and considered likely to achieve their goals.
transcript.translation: 总体而言，充满热情的人往往被正面看待，被认为更有可能实现自己的目标。

transcript.text: But when it comes to predicting achievement, has the importance of passion been overstated?
transcript.translation: 但在预测成就时，热情的重要性是否被夸大了呢？

transcript.text: According to a new study from Stanford University, passion may be less important in certain cultures.
transcript.translation: 根据斯坦福大学的一项新研究，在某些文化中，热情或许没那么重要。

transcript.text: And the fact that passion is often seen as a key to achievement may reflect a distinctly Western model of motivation.
transcript.translation: 而热情常被视为成功关键这一现象，可能反映的是一种典型的西方式动机模式。

transcript.text: The chief factor explored in the study was how individualistic a society was.
transcript.translation: 这项研究探讨的主要因素是一个社会的个人主义程度。

transcript.text: In individualistic cultures, the researchers assert, people are more motivated by pursuing paths related to their passions.
transcript.translation: 研究者指出，在个人主义文化中，人们更倾向于因追求与自身热情相关的道路而受到激励。

transcript.text: But those in collectivistic cultures are more likely to see themselves as part of a network.
transcript.translation: 而集体主义文化中的人则更倾向于把自己看作某个关系网络的一部分。

transcript.text: They often place fulfilling obligations to others above focusing on their own interests.
transcript.translation: 他们常常把履行对他人的义务置于关注自身兴趣之上。

transcript.text: The researchers looked at data from nearly 60 countries.
transcript.translation: 研究者分析了来自近六十个国家的数据。

transcript.text: They found that, in science subjects, passion was positively correlated with academic achievements.
transcript.translation: 他们发现，在理科科目中，热情与学业成绩呈正相关。

transcript.text: Higher levels of enjoyment and interest also bolstered test scores.
transcript.translation: 更高的乐趣和兴趣水平也能提升考试成绩。

transcript.text: But the strength of this correlation wasn't the same across cultures.
transcript.translation: 但这种相关性的强弱在不同文化中并不相同。

transcript.text: Those in individualistic societies, such as the US, Australia, and the UK, showed a stronger link between passion and achievement.
transcript.translation: 在美国、澳大利亚和英国等个人主义社会中，热情与成就之间的关联更强。

transcript.text: The effect of passion on performance was more subtle for those in more collectivistic societies such as Colombia or Thailand.
transcript.translation: 对于哥伦比亚或泰国等更具集体主义色彩的社会，激情对成绩的影响则更为微妙。

transcript.text: These findings were mirrored in achievement in both mathematics and reading.
transcript.translation: 这些发现在数学和阅读的成绩中同样得到了印证。

transcript.text: It's clear from the findings that passion isn't the only thing that motivates people to achieve their goals.
transcript.translation: 从这些发现可以清楚地看出，热情并不是激励人们实现目标的唯一因素。

transcript.text: Why does nature create patterns?
transcript.translation: 大自然为什么会创造出各种图案？

transcript.text: The reason patterns often appear in nature is simple.
transcript.translation: 图案之所以常出现在自然界，原因其实很简单。

transcript.text: The same basic physical or chemical processes occur in many patterned substances and organisms as they form.
transcript.translation: 许多带有图案的物质和生物在形成时，都经历着相同的基本物理或化学过程。

transcript.text: Whether in plants and animals or rocks, foams, and ice crystals, the intricate patterns that happen in nature come down to what's happening at the level of atoms and molecules.
transcript.translation: 无论是在动植物身上，还是在岩石、泡沫和冰晶中，自然界中出现的这些精巧图案，归根结底都取决于原子和分子层面所发生的变化。

transcript.text: A pattern in nature is any regularly repeated arrangement of shapes or colors.
transcript.translation: 自然界中的图案，指的是任何有规律地重复排列的形状或颜色。

transcript.text: Some of the most striking examples include the six-sided arrays of rocks at Giant's Causeway in the United Kingdom and the colorful stripes and spots on tropical fish.
transcript.translation: 一些最引人注目的例子包括英国巨人堤道上六边形排列的岩石，以及热带鱼身上彩色的条纹和斑点。

transcript.text: Patterns like these begin to form at a small scale when materials undergo processes like drying, freezing, wrinkling, diffusing, and reacting.
transcript.translation: 当物质经历干燥、冷冻、起皱、扩散和反应等过程时，这类图案便开始在微观尺度上形成。

transcript.text: These changes then give rise to complex patterns at a larger scale that people can see.
transcript.translation: 这些变化随后在更大的、人们肉眼可见的尺度上形成复杂的图案。

transcript.text: Imagine delicate frozen crystals on a window during winter.
transcript.translation: 想象一下冬天窗户上那些精致的冰晶。

transcript.text: What creates that pattern?
transcript.translation: 是什么造就了那样的图案呢？

transcript.text: When water freezes, its molecules begin clustering together.
transcript.translation: 水结冰时，它的分子开始聚集成团。

transcript.text: Water molecules have a particular bent shape that causes them to stack into clusters as they freeze.
transcript.translation: 水分子具有一种特殊的弯曲形状，这使它们在结冰时会堆叠成团簇。

transcript.text: As the cluster grows, many outside factors, including humidity and temperature, begin to affect its overall shape.
transcript.translation: 随着团簇不断增大，包括湿度和温度在内的许多外部因素开始影响它的整体形状。

transcript.text: If the water is freezing on a window, for example, random imperfections on the glass surface affect the stacking and create the larger pattern.
transcript.translation: 举例来说，如果水是在窗户上结冰，玻璃表面随机的瑕疵就会影响分子的堆叠方式，从而形成更大的图案。

transcript.text: But scientists do not always know the purpose of a pattern, or even if there is one.
transcript.translation: 但科学家并不总是知道某种图案的用途，甚至不确定它是否真有用途。

transcript.text: The molecular processes involved are simple enough that they might generate a pattern by coincidence.
transcript.translation: 其中涉及的分子过程足够简单，因此它们有可能只是偶然生成了某种图案。

transcript.text: Many people, myself included, have multiple areas of life they would like to improve.
transcript.translation: 很多人，包括我自己在内，都有生活中多个想要改善的方面。

transcript.text: For example, I would like to reach more people with my writing, to lift heavier weights at the gym, and to start practicing mindfulness more consistently.
transcript.translation: 比如，我希望自己的写作能触及更多的人，希望在健身房举起更重的重量，也希望能更持续地练习正念。

transcript.text: Those are just a few of the goals I find desirable, and you probably have a long list yourself.
transcript.translation: 这些只是我想要实现的几个目标，而你自己大概也有长长的一串。

transcript.text: The problem is, even if we are committed to working hard on our goals, our natural tendency is to return to our old habits at some point.
transcript.translation: 问题在于，即便我们下定决心为目标努力，我们的天性还是会在某个时刻让我们回到旧习惯。

transcript.text: Making a permanent lifestyle change is really difficult.
transcript.translation: 要做出一次持久的生活方式改变真的很难。

transcript.text: Recently, I've come across a few studies that will make these difficult lifestyle changes a bit easier.
transcript.translation: 最近，我读到了几项研究，它们能让这些艰难的生活方式改变变得容易一些。

transcript.text: As you'll see, however, the approach to mastering many areas of life is somewhat counter-intuitive.
transcript.translation: 不过，正如你将看到的，掌控生活中诸多方面的方法有些违反直觉。

transcript.text: Research has shown that you are two to three times more likely to stick with your habits if you make a specific plan for when, where and how you will perform the behaviour.
transcript.translation: 研究表明，如果你为自己何时、何地以及如何执行某个行为制定了具体计划，那么你坚持这一习惯的可能性会提高两到三倍。

transcript.text: For example, in one study, scientists asked people to fill out a sentence to specify during the next week they would do at least 20 minutes of vigorous exercise on which day, at what time of day, and at or in what place.
transcript.translation: 例如，在一项研究中，科学家让人们填写一个句子，具体写明在接下来的一周里，他们会在哪一天、一天中的什么时间、在什么地点进行至少二十分钟的剧烈运动。

transcript.text: Researchers found that people who filled out this sentence were two to three times more likely to actually exercise compared to a control group who did not make plans for their future behaviour.
transcript.translation: 研究者发现，与没有为未来行为制定计划的对照组相比，填写了这个句子的人真正去运动的可能性要高出两到三倍。

transcript.text: Psychologists call these specific plans implementation intentions, because they state when, where and how you intend to implement a particular behaviour.
transcript.translation: 心理学家把这些具体的计划称为'执行意图'，因为它们说明了你打算在何时、何地以及如何执行某个特定行为。

transcript.text: However, follow-up research has discovered implementation intentions only work when you focus on one thing at a time.
transcript.translation: 然而，后续研究发现，只有当你一次专注于一件事时，执行意图才会奏效。

transcript.text: In fact, researchers found that people who tried to accomplish multiple goals were less committed and less likely to succeed than those who focused on a single goal.
transcript.translation: 事实上，研究者发现，与专注于单一目标的人相比，试图同时实现多个目标的人投入程度更低，成功的可能性也更小。

transcript.text: Another science-based reason to focus on one thing at a time is that when you begin practising a new habit, it requires a lot of conscious effort to remember to do it.
transcript.translation: 一次只专注一件事还有另一个基于科学的理由：当你开始培养一个新习惯时，需要付出大量有意识的努力才能记得去做。

transcript.text: After a while, however, the pattern of behaviour becomes easier.
transcript.translation: 但过了一段时间，这种行为模式就会变得轻松起来。

transcript.text: Eventually, your new habit becomes a normal routine and the process is more or less mindless and automatic.
transcript.translation: 最终，你的新习惯会变成一种日常惯例，整个过程或多或少变得无需思考、自动完成。

transcript.text: The most important thing to note is that there is some tipping point at which new habits become more or less automatic.
transcript.translation: 最需要注意的是，存在某个临界点，一旦越过，新习惯就会或多或少地变得自动化。

transcript.text: The time it takes to build a habit depends on many factors, including how difficult the habit is, your genetics and more.
transcript.translation: 养成一个习惯所需的时间取决于许多因素，包括这个习惯的难度、你的基因等等。

transcript.text: It was a lazy, hazy, crazy day on the dwarf planet Pluto when New Horizons, a spacecraft from Earth, flew by at a speed of 31,000 miles per hour two years ago.
transcript.translation: 两年前，当来自地球的'新视野号'探测器以每小时三万一千英里的速度飞掠矮行星冥王星时，那是冥王星上慵懒、朦胧而又疯狂的一天。

transcript.text: The spacecraft took a bunch of photos, made some quick measurements of Pluto's atmosphere and sent them all back here, giving planetary scientists their first up-close look of the distant dwarf planet.
transcript.translation: 这艘探测器拍下了一批照片，对冥王星的大气进行了一些快速测量，并把这些数据全部传回地球，让行星科学家第一次近距离观察到这颗遥远的矮行星。

transcript.text: One of the more bizarre things they found was that the haze in Pluto's atmosphere was much thicker than previously thought.
transcript.translation: 他们发现的较为离奇的现象之一，是冥王星大气中的雾霾比先前所认为的要浓厚得多。

transcript.text: The planet also had an atmosphere much cooler than earlier estimates, topping out at minus 333.4 degrees Fahrenheit.
transcript.translation: 这颗星球的大气也比早先估计的要冷得多，最高温度仅为零下333.4华氏度。

transcript.text: Now a study published in Nature links those two atmospheric observations.
transcript.translation: 如今，一项发表在《自然》杂志上的研究把这两项大气观测结果联系了起来。

transcript.text: A computer model developed by planetary scientist Xi Zang and colleagues shows the haze of tiny droplets in the upper atmosphere is likely scattering light from the sun, preventing heat from reaching the planet below.
transcript.translation: 由行星科学家张希及其同事建立的计算机模型显示，高层大气中由微小液滴组成的雾霾很可能正在散射来自太阳的光线，阻止热量抵达下方的星球表面。

transcript.text: We see hazy skies on Earth too from time to time, whenever solid particles get suspended in the air, from water-based fogs to ash from fires to the toxic droplets that make up a thick smog.
transcript.translation: 我们在地球上也时常会看到雾蒙蒙的天空，只要有固体颗粒悬浮在空气中就会如此，从水汽形成的雾，到火灾产生的灰烬，再到构成浓重雾霾的有毒液滴，都是这样。

transcript.text: But on Earth the overall temperature of the planet is dominated by the distribution of gases in our atmosphere.
transcript.translation: 但在地球上，整个星球的温度主要由大气中气体的分布所决定。

transcript.text: On Pluto, the authors suggest, haze might be more influential.
transcript.translation: 而在冥王星上，作者们认为，雾霾的影响可能更大。

transcript.text: Particles can reflect light from the sun here on Earth.
transcript.translation: 在地球上，颗粒物能够反射来自太阳的光线。

transcript.text: It happens after volcanoes erupt, emitting clouds of particles that reflect the sun's rays into the atmosphere.
transcript.translation: 这种情况会在火山喷发后发生，火山喷出的颗粒云会把太阳光反射回大气层中。

transcript.text: Some people even propose imitating this phenomenon to alleviate the effects of climate change.
transcript.translation: 有些人甚至提议模仿这一现象来缓解气候变化的影响。

transcript.text: But our planet isn't dominated by that process, or at least it hasn't been for a few billion years.
transcript.translation: 但我们这颗星球并不受那种过程主导，或者至少几十亿年来一直不是。

transcript.text: If Pluto's atmosphere is very different from ours, and from that of other nearby planets, it could help scientists expand their understanding of planetary atmospheres.
transcript.translation: 如果冥王星的大气与我们的以及附近其他行星的大气差别很大，那么它有助于科学家拓展对行星大气的理解。

transcript.text: But right now this is just a good guess, based on data from New Horizons and a sophisticated computer model, not direct observations of the haze's composition.
transcript.translation: 但目前这只是一个不错的猜测，它基于'新视野号'的数据和一个复杂的计算机模型，而非对雾霾成分的直接观测。

transcript.text: There are other theories floating around to explain Pluto's cool temperatures, including blaming the cold air on gases in the atmosphere.
transcript.translation: 还有其他一些理论在试图解释冥王星的低温，包括把寒冷的空气归因于大气中的气体。

transcript.text: Luckily, the authors will get a chance to test their notions when the James Webb Space Telescope launches later.
transcript.translation: 幸运的是，等到詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜日后发射时，作者们将有机会检验他们的设想。

transcript.text: That observatory can detect different spectrums of light, which the hazy Plutonian atmosphere would be positively glowing with, as it's scattered sunlight.
transcript.translation: 那台天文台能探测不同波段的光谱，朦胧的冥王星大气因散射阳光会在这些光谱中明显发亮。

transcript.text: The researchers just have to wait and see if the light from the telescope validates their bright idea.
transcript.translation: 研究者们只需拭目以待，看看望远镜接收到的光是否会证实他们这个绝妙的想法。

transcript.text: Parents have a small window where they can influence their 8-10 year old children's music taste, researchers have concluded.
transcript.translation: 研究人员得出结论，父母有一个短暂的时间窗口，可以影响8到10岁孩子的音乐品味。

transcript.text: The 24-month time frame comes at an age when youngsters are old enough to appreciate poetic lyrics and snappy tunes, but have not yet started to be embarrassed by their mother and father's preferences.
transcript.translation: 这个为期24个月的时间段所处的年龄，孩子们已经大到能够欣赏优美的歌词和明快的旋律，却还没有开始因为父母的喜好而感到难为情。

transcript.text: Dr. Hawke Eggerman, a lecturer in music at the University of York, carried out a literature review into more than a dozen studies looking at parental musical influence.
transcript.translation: 约克大学的音乐讲师 Hawke Eggerman 博士对十几项探讨父母音乐影响力的研究进行了文献综述。

transcript.text: Children have an openness to new music, and this means parents have an important role to play in developing the musical preferences of their kids, he said.
transcript.translation: 他说，孩子们对新音乐持开放态度，这意味着父母在培养孩子的音乐偏好方面发挥着重要作用。

transcript.text: However, time is of the essence, as parental influence is most likely to be effective during the critical time period before age 10.
transcript.translation: 然而，时机至关重要，因为父母的影响最有可能在孩子10岁之前这一关键时期发挥作用。

transcript.text: During adolescence, children tend to gravitate away from their parents' choices and are more influenced by their peers.
transcript.translation: 进入青春期后，孩子们往往会逐渐偏离父母的选择，转而更多地受到同龄人的影响。

transcript.text: A separate survey of 2,000 British parents by music streaming service, Deezer, also found that nearly four-fifths of parents agreed that their children were far more receptive to their musical suggestions before the age of 10.
transcript.translation: 音乐流媒体服务 Deezer 针对2000名英国父母开展的另一项调查也发现，近五分之四的父母认为，孩子在10岁之前对他们的音乐推荐要容易接受得多。

transcript.text: In contrast, just 10% of parents reported positive reactions from their teenage children when they shared their favourite music.
transcript.translation: 相比之下，只有10%的父母表示，当他们与十几岁的孩子分享自己喜欢的音乐时，得到了积极的反应。

transcript.text: Some 79% of fathers said they had tried to influence their children's music, but just 69% of mothers.
transcript.translation: 约有79%的父亲表示曾试图影响孩子的音乐品味，而母亲这一比例仅为69%。

transcript.text: However, mothers were more effective, with 38% reporting that their kids loved the tunes they shared, compared to 30% of dads who in some cases said their children cried or even fell asleep.
transcript.translation: 不过，母亲的效果更好，有38%的母亲表示孩子喜欢她们分享的曲子，而父亲这一比例为30%，有些父亲甚至说孩子听了会哭，或者干脆睡着了。

transcript.text: Dr. Eggerman claims introducing children to a variety of musical styles is the key to fostering good taste in later life.
transcript.translation: Eggerman 博士认为，让孩子接触多种音乐风格，是日后培养良好音乐品味的关键。

transcript.text: By playing children a variety of genres before this critical period, research on familiarization suggests they will enjoy lots of different types of music as adults he added.
transcript.translation: 他补充说，有关熟悉度的研究表明，在这一关键时期之前给孩子播放各种类型的音乐，他们成年后就会喜欢许多不同类型的音乐。

transcript.text: The benefits of having a wider taste in music include the ability to manage their emotions more effectively, socialise and bond with others more easily, and to have a better understanding of other cultures as well.
transcript.translation: 拥有更广泛音乐品味的好处包括：能更有效地管理自己的情绪，更容易与他人交往和建立情感联系，以及对其他文化也有更深的理解。

transcript.text: Dr. Eggerman advises parents not to push their favourite music too hard on their children, but instead play it as background music while a child is playing.
transcript.translation: Eggerman 博士建议父母不要过于强硬地把自己喜欢的音乐塞给孩子，而应在孩子玩耍时把它作为背景音乐播放。

transcript.text: They can also help create positive memories about artists and bands by going to concerts and live music events together.
transcript.translation: 他们还可以通过一起去听音乐会和现场演出，帮助孩子建立起对歌手和乐队的美好记忆。

paragraphs.text: Imagine you and a stranger are sitting on a couch. How close would you sit to them? It turns out that how much of a __26__ zone you prefer may reveal a lot about your personality.
paragraphs.translation: 想象一下你和一个陌生人坐在同一张沙发上。你会和对方坐得多近？事实证明，你偏好留出多大的缓冲区，可能透露出许多关于你性格的信息。

paragraphs.text: In one study, researchers sought to __27__ how our personality may be linked to our preferred amount of personal space. The researchers found that people who scored higher in the __28__ of agreeableness tended to sit closer to others, as did people who were more open and outgoing.
paragraphs.translation: 在一项研究中，研究人员试图弄清楚我们的性格如何与我们偏好的个人空间大小相关联。研究人员发现，在'宜人性'这一人格特质上得分更高的人往往会与他人坐得更近，性格更开放、更外向的人也是如此。

paragraphs.text: Other individual differences, such as gender and age, can also affect how much personal space we __29__. Women tend to prefer more physical distance from strangers or acquaintances and older adults also generally tend to prefer to keep more distance between themselves and others.
paragraphs.translation: 其他个体差异，比如性别和年龄，也会影响我们渴望多大的个人空间。女性往往偏好与陌生人或熟人保持更大的身体距离，年长者通常也倾向于在自己与他人之间保持更大的距离。

paragraphs.text: Beyond reflecting our personality and __30__, the amount of personal space we prefer is also linked to our cultural backgrounds. In a study involving participants from 42 countries, researchers found that around the world people's desired amount of personal space varied __31__. For example, in Romania, the average amount of personal space people said they would prefer from a stranger was more than 4 feet, whereas in Argentina it was roughly half that.
paragraphs.translation: 除了反映我们的性格和人口统计特征之外，我们偏好的个人空间大小还与文化背景有关。在一项涉及来自42个国家参与者的研究中，研究人员发现，世界各地人们期望的个人空间大小差异很大。例如，在罗马尼亚，人们表示希望与陌生人保持的平均个人空间超过4英尺，而在阿根廷则大约只有其一半。

paragraphs.text: What might __32__ this variation? The researchers looked at a number of __33__ factors, but the only one that was significantly __34__ with preferred interpersonal distance was average temperature. The warmer the place, it seems, the "warmer" the people and the less space they needed between others.
paragraphs.translation: 这种差异背后可能有什么原因？研究人员考察了一系列潜在因素，但唯一与偏好的人际距离显著相关的因素是平均气温。似乎气候越温暖的地方，人们越'热情'，彼此之间需要的空间也就越小。

paragraphs.text: Personal space may also reflect interpersonal attraction. Researchers have found that our chosen physical __35__ also appears to reflect how much we like others. The more people would like to be friends with the other person, the closer they sat to them.
paragraphs.translation: 个人空间也可能反映人际吸引力。研究人员发现，我们所选择的身体距离似乎也反映了我们对他人的喜爱程度。越是想与对方成为朋友的人，坐得离对方就越近。

questionGroups.title: It's never too early to teach children about money

material.title: It's never too early to teach children about money

paragraphs.text: The cost of a mortgage or rents, meeting monthly utility bills, paying for a new car—all headaches most people get to worry about from their 20s. But while some may struggle to pay their bills after a few too many nights out at the start of the month, others will have a tightly followed plan for their repayments. So what is the difference between the shrewd saver and the more reckless spender?
paragraphs.translation: 房贷或房租、每月的水电费、买新车——这些都是大多数人从二十几岁起就要操心的烦心事。但有些人在月初出去玩了几个晚上后可能连账单都难以支付，另一些人却对自己的还款有着严格执行的计划。那么，精明的储蓄者与更加挥霍的消费者之间的区别究竟是什么？

paragraphs.text: Experts believe it is all about the age you learn how to spend responsibly. Adult money habits are typically set by the age of seven, according to a large-scale study by the government's Money Advice Service and behaviour experts at Cambridge University. By then, most children have grasped how to recognise the value of money and are capable of complex functions such as planning ahead, delaying a decision until later and understanding that some choices are irreversible.
paragraphs.translation: 专家认为，这一切都取决于你学会负责任地花钱的年龄。根据政府的理财咨询服务机构和剑桥大学行为专家开展的一项大规模研究，成年人的金钱习惯通常在七岁时就已定型。到那时，大多数儿童已经掌握了如何认识金钱的价值，并能够完成诸如提前规划、推迟做决定，以及理解某些选择不可逆转等复杂行为。

paragraphs.text: Tomorrow marks the start of Global Money Week, a worldwide initiative to help children make smart financial decisions and learn that "money matters matter". But for many young people in the UK, it's a matter of too little, too late. "The habits of mind which influence the ways children approach complex problems and decisions, including financial ones, are largely determined in the first few years of life," says Dr David Whitebread, the co-author of the study. And this core behaviour is very likely to influence their financial decisions when they are adults, he says.
paragraphs.translation: 明天是'全球理财周'的开始，这是一项旨在帮助儿童做出明智财务决策、并让他们懂得'钱的事很重要'的全球性倡议。但对英国许多年轻人而言，这来得太少、太晚。'影响儿童处理复杂问题和决策（包括财务决策）方式的思维习惯，在很大程度上是在生命最初几年里形成的，'该研究的合著者 David Whitebread 博士说。他说，这一核心行为很可能会影响他们成年后的财务决策。

paragraphs.text: The study also urges parents not to underestimate their own good and bad money habits. "Since young children have few monetary resources they control independently, it is the basic approaches and skills which are modelled, discussed and demonstrated by parents that are likely to be influential levers, breeding efficient habits and practices," it says.
paragraphs.translation: 该研究还敦促父母不要低估自己好的和坏的金钱习惯。'由于幼儿几乎没有能够独立支配的金钱资源，因此真正可能成为有影响力杠杆、培养出高效习惯与做法的，是父母所示范、讨论和展示的基本方法与技能，'研究写道。

paragraphs.text: Parents who choose to help their children learn how to plan ahead, reflect on the past and self-regulate can make a huge difference in promoting good financial behaviour in the future, explains Whitebread. According to a survey by M&G Investments, the vast majority (83%) of parents recognise the value of teaching their children about money. However, this concern does not always carry through to practice—one in six do not feel confident enough to do it. More than one in every four parents think children should take responsibility for understanding money themselves.
paragraphs.translation: Whitebread 解释说，选择帮助孩子学会提前规划、反思过去和自我约束的父母，能够在未来培养良好财务行为方面产生巨大影响。根据 M&G Investments 的一项调查，绝大多数（83%）父母认识到教孩子理财的价值。然而，这种关注并不总能落实到行动上——六分之一的父母对此没有足够信心。超过四分之一的父母认为，孩子应该自己承担理解金钱的责任。

paragraphs.text: "There's joy in the fact that young children are spontaneous and live life in the moment, unrestrained by adult problems. But teaching children about money when they are young is a good way for parents to help them learn to delay satisfaction, so that the child thinks: 'I'd like to do this but I'm not going to'. Hard evidence suggests, if you want your child to do well in life, the earlier you can start trying to teach them inhibition and self-discipline, the better," says Whitebread, pointing to research that has shown people in prison frequently have poor impulse control, a personality trait that can affect relationships and long-term health.
paragraphs.translation: '幼儿天真自然、活在当下、不受成年人烦恼束缚，这本身就是一种快乐。但在孩子小时候教他们理财，是父母帮助他们学会延迟满足的好方法，这样孩子就会想：我很想这么做，但我不打算这么做。确凿证据表明，如果你希望孩子将来生活顺遂，越早开始尝试教他们自我克制和自律越好，' Whitebread 说。他指出，有研究显示监狱中的人往往冲动控制能力差，而这是一种会影响人际关系和长期健康的性格特质。

paragraphs.text: But how should a parent try to teach their child to spend responsibly? One simple way is to give them pocket money and then help them to analyse and learn from any foolish spending decisions.
paragraphs.translation: 那么，父母应该如何试着教孩子负责任地花钱呢？一个简单的办法是给他们零花钱，然后帮助他们分析并从任何愚蠢的消费决定中吸取教训。

paragraphs.text: Another is through board games which can help teach financial responsibility. Pop to the Shops, a shopping board game for five-to-nine-year-olds, has been one of Orchard Toys' top 10 bestselling board games every year for the past 15 years. To win, players must use fake coins to purchase everyday grocery items from various shops around the board, and give the other players who visit their shop the correct change. If they don't have enough money, they must purchase a cheaper item. "It acts as a conversation starter about money—parents can fill in the gaps," says Orchard Toys product manager Rachael Sutcliffe.
paragraphs.translation: 另一个办法是通过桌游来帮助教导财务责任。Pop to the Shops 是一款面向5到9岁儿童的购物桌游，过去15年里每年都跻身 Orchard Toys 最畅销桌游前十名。要想获胜，玩家必须用假硬币从棋盘上各家商店购买日常杂货，并给到访自己商店的其他玩家找回正确的零钱。如果钱不够，他们就必须购买更便宜的商品。'它能引出关于金钱的话题——父母可以从旁补充讲解，' Orchard Toys 产品经理 Rachael Sutcliffe 说。

paragraphs.text: There are also some pocket-money-tracking and payment apps, such as RoosterMoney and goHenry, which are designed to be used by under-sevens, and which boast that they can help children develop good money habits. This is dependent on the children receiving enough pocket money to need an app to track their spending, which research suggests is not always the case.
paragraphs.translation: 还有一些零花钱追踪和支付应用，比如 RoosterMoney 和 goHenry，它们专为七岁以下儿童设计，号称能帮助孩子养成良好的金钱习惯。不过这取决于孩子是否能拿到足够多的零花钱，以至于需要一个应用来追踪支出，而研究表明情况并非总是如此。

paragraphs.text: Surprisingly, given the research about habit-forming in young children, there are very few gaming apps that can help under-sevens—Pigby's Fair, developed by NatWest, being a notable exception. In this, children who solve basic puzzles will earn virtual money selling what they have made at different stalls in a fair, then spend or save it. But the need to shift virtual money around, and take into account interest payments and pocket money bonuses, makes it a complex financial education tool.
paragraphs.translation: 令人意外的是，鉴于有关幼儿习惯养成的研究，能帮助七岁以下儿童的游戏类应用却少之又少——由 NatWest 开发的 Pigby's Fair 是一个显著的例外。在这款应用里，解决基础谜题的孩子会通过在集市不同摊位上出售自己制作的东西来赚取虚拟货币，然后花掉或存起来。但由于需要调配虚拟货币，并考虑利息支付和零花钱奖励，它成了一个复杂的财商教育工具。

paragraphs.text: There are plenty of online games which focus on coin recognition and counting with money, such as the Igloo Shopping game or Top Marks' Coins Game. So what if children find such games boring? An exciting (and free) real-world option for parents to use is a visit to Metro Bank. Although, like most banks, it does not allow children to open an account until they turn 11, it specifically tries to offer young children a chance to learn about money inside its branches by inviting kids to use the "magic money machines" to count their coins. Children who accurately guess how much was in their piggy bank (猪形储钱罐) get a prize, and free candies are handed out when the coins are exchanged for banknotes. The bank does not take a commission from the transaction.
paragraphs.translation: 有许多在线游戏专注于硬币识别和数钱，比如 Igloo Shopping 游戏或 Top Marks 的 Coins Game。那么如果孩子觉得这类游戏无聊怎么办？一个令父母兴奋（而且免费）的现实选择是去 Metro Bank 参观。虽然和大多数银行一样，它要到孩子11岁才允许开户，但它专门尝试通过邀请孩子使用'魔法数钱机'来数硬币，让幼儿在其分行内了解金钱。准确猜出自己猪形储钱罐里有多少钱的孩子会获得奖品，而当硬币兑换成纸币时还会免费派发糖果。银行不从该交易中收取佣金。

paragraphs.text: At six years old, my daughter Flora is getting to grips with her finances early. She tested out a number of games aimed at teaching children her age the value of money. She enjoyed them all, but best, in her view, is Money Match Cafe, a board game where she must work out the value of different denominations (面额) of coin in her imaginary restaurant, her "customers" being her stuffed toys. "It was really fun because you get to serve food to your own toys on a little tray with a napkin on it, and then you can hug them," she says.
paragraphs.translation: 我六岁的女儿 Flora 很早就开始学着打理自己的'财务'。她试玩了许多旨在教她这个年龄段孩子认识金钱价值的游戏。她全都喜欢，但在她看来最好的是 Money Match Cafe，这是一款桌游，她必须在自己想象中的餐厅里算出不同面额硬币的价值，她的'顾客'就是她的毛绒玩具。'这真的很有趣，因为你可以把食物放在铺着餐巾的小托盘上端给自己的玩具，然后还能抱抱它们，'她说。

paragraphs.text: "If you're six and you play this game, you'll learn that you might not have the right amount of money for what you want to buy. You just have to cross your fingers and hope. It's a good challenge, and I enjoyed adding the coins up to see how much they made. But I don't like the name. Money Match Cafe is not a good name for a café. I would have liked it more if it had been Flora's Cafe or Fantastically Baked Lunches."
paragraphs.translation: '如果你六岁玩这个游戏，你会明白你想买的东西也许钱不够。你只能双手交叉、寄希望于运气。这是个不错的挑战，我很喜欢把硬币加起来看看总共有多少。但我不喜欢这个名字。Money Match Cafe 不是一个咖啡馆的好名字。如果它叫 Flora's Cafe 或 Fantastically Baked Lunches，我会更喜欢它。'

paragraphs.text: Seven out of ten teachers think children are now faced with financial decisions earlier. On Wednesday, Lifesavers—a new project which promotes financial education in primary schools—is hosting a conference to encourage teachers to join its programme and get free classroom resources and training. Almost two-thirds of millennials (千禧一代) wish they had received more money advice at a younger age, according to a Santander survey.
paragraphs.translation: 十位教师中有七位认为，如今孩子们更早地面临财务决策。周三，Lifesavers——一个在小学推广财商教育的新项目——将举办一场会议，鼓励教师加入其计划并获得免费的课堂资源和培训。根据桑坦德银行的一项调查，近三分之二的千禧一代希望自己能在更小的年纪得到更多理财建议。

paragraphs.text: Only a third of parents involve their children in discussions about their household finances, even though less than half of young people aged seven to seventeen receive financial education at school, another survey shows.
paragraphs.translation: 另一项调查显示，只有三分之一的父母会让孩子参与关于家庭财务的讨论，尽管七到十七岁的年轻人中只有不到一半在学校接受过财商教育。

paragraphs.text: Most adults believe their parents have had the biggest influence on their money behaviour. So when should they start trying to instil (灌输) good habits? As early as possible before the age of seven, research suggests.
paragraphs.translation: 大多数成年人认为，父母对他们金钱行为的影响最大。那么，他们应该在什么时候开始尝试灌输良好习惯呢？研究表明，越早越好，最好在七岁之前。

questionGroups.directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.statementText: Most parents realise the importance of teaching their children how to handle money, but many of them actually don't do much in this respect.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 E。段落 E 指出绝大多数（83%）父母认识到教孩子理财的价值，'However, this concern does not always carry through to practice'（这种关注并不总能落实到行动上），与陈述中'realise the importance... but many of them actually don't do much'吻合。

questions.statementText: People differ substantially in their way of managing finance.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 A。段落 A 对比了'struggle to pay their bills'的人与'have a tightly followed plan'的人，并以'the difference between the shrewd saver and the more reckless spender'收束，说明人们理财方式差异很大，与陈述一致。

questions.statementText: Parents can easily teach children how to spend responsibly by helping them draw lessons from bad decisions on spending.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 G。段落 G 提出给孩子零花钱，然后'help them to analyse and learn from any foolish spending decisions'（帮他们分析并从愚蠢消费决定中吸取教训），与陈述吻合。

questions.statementText: Many young British people badly lack money management skills and they don't learn them early enough.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 C。段落 C 指出对英国许多年轻人而言理财教育'too little, too late'（太少、太晚），且理财思维习惯在生命最初几年就已决定，与陈述中'lack money management skills and don't learn them early enough'一致。

questions.statementText: The majority of adults believe that their spending habits have been influenced the most by their parents.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 P。段落 P 首句'Most adults believe their parents have had the biggest influence on their money behaviour'与陈述几乎逐词对应。

questions.statementText: There are apps designed specifically for children under 7 to help them track pocket money spending.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 I。段落 I 提到 RoosterMoney、goHenry 等'pocket-money-tracking... apps... designed to be used by under-sevens'，与陈述吻合。

questions.statementText: According to experts, the age a person learns to manage finance responsibly determines the way they handle money thereafter.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 B。段落 B 指出'Experts believe it is all about the age you learn how to spend responsibly'，且成人金钱习惯七岁定型，与陈述一致。

questions.statementText: Most teachers are of the opinion that children today need to make financial decisions at a younger age.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 N。段落 N 首句'Seven out of ten teachers think children are now faced with financial decisions earlier'与陈述吻合。

questions.statementText: Parents serve as effective role models in shaping children's money management habits.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 D。段落 D 强调正是父母所'modelled, discussed and demonstrated'的基本方法与技能成为'influential levers, breeding efficient habits'，即父母作为榜样塑造孩子的理财习惯，与陈述一致。

questions.statementText: According to one study, about 30% of parents allow their children to participate in discussions on their family finances.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 O。段落 O 指出'Only a third of parents involve their children in discussions about their household finances'（只有约三分之一的父母让孩子参与家庭财务讨论），与陈述吻合。

questionGroups.title: Passage 1

paragraphs.text: Three artists have brought a lawsuit against Stability AI, DeviantArt, and Midjourney, alleging that the text-to-image AI tools have infringed the rights of thousands of artists.
paragraphs.translation: 三位艺术家对 Stability AI、DeviantArt 和 Midjourney 提起诉讼，指控这些文本生成图像的 AI 工具侵犯了成千上万名艺术家的权利。

paragraphs.text: The lawsuit claims that the Stable Diffusion tool used by Stability AI, DeviantArt, and Midjourney was trained on billions of copyrighted images downloaded from the internet and used by the companies "without compensation or consent from the artists."
paragraphs.translation: 该诉讼声称，Stability AI、DeviantArt 和 Midjourney 所使用的 Stable Diffusion 工具，是在从互联网下载的数十亿张受版权保护的图像上训练的，而这些公司使用这些图像'既未向艺术家支付报酬，也未取得其同意'。

paragraphs.text: The artists are represented by The Joseph Saveri Law Firm and Matthew Butterick.
paragraphs.translation: 这些艺术家由 Joseph Saveri 律师事务所和 Matthew Butterick 代理。

paragraphs.text: "If Stable Diffusion and similar products are allowed to continue to operate as they do now, the foreseeable result is they will replace the very artists whose stolen works power these AI products with whom they are competing," the law firm wrote in a press release. "AI image products are not just an infringement of artists' rights; they will eliminate 'artist' as a viable career path. In addition to obtaining compensation for the wrongful conduct, this lawsuit seeks to prevent that outcome and ensure these products follow the same rules as any other new technology that involves the use of massive amounts of intellectual property. If streaming music can be accomplished within the law, so can AI products."
paragraphs.translation: '如果允许 Stable Diffusion 及类似产品继续像现在这样运作，可预见的结果就是：它们将取代那些作品被窃取、用来驱动这些 AI 产品的艺术家本身，而这些艺术家正是它们的竞争对手，'该律师事务所在一份新闻稿中写道。'AI 图像产品不仅仅是对艺术家权利的侵犯，它们还会让“艺术家”这一可行的职业道路彻底消失。除了为这一不当行为寻求赔偿，本诉讼还力图阻止这一结果，并确保这些产品遵守与任何其他涉及大量使用知识产权的新技术相同的规则。如果流媒体音乐能够在法律框架内实现，AI 产品也同样可以。'

paragraphs.text: Since text-to-image generators have increased in popularity in the past year, many artists have been vocalizing their opposition to AI art after seeing their own distorted signatures appear in AI art and finding out that their work was used to train the tools without their permission.
paragraphs.translation: 自过去一年文本生成图像的工具日益流行以来，许多艺术家在看到自己被扭曲的签名出现在 AI 艺术作品中、并发现自己的作品未经许可就被用于训练这些工具后，纷纷公开表达对 AI 艺术的反对。

paragraphs.text: Not only are many artists furious at the possible copyright violations of AI art, but they have also been frustrated by how AI tools are able to sidestep the labor and art processes they are required to go through. As a result, many artists have been trying to ban AI art from art-sharing platforms.
paragraphs.translation: 许多艺术家不仅对 AI 艺术可能存在的版权侵犯行为感到愤怒，还对 AI 工具能够绕过他们必须经历的劳动与创作过程感到沮丧。因此，许多艺术家一直试图将 AI 艺术从艺术分享平台上封禁。

paragraphs.text: As AI innovation continues at a rapid speed, it seems that artists and lawmakers are trying to put a brake on further developments before it's too late.
paragraphs.translation: 随着 AI 创新以飞快的速度持续推进，艺术家和立法者似乎正试图在为时已晚之前，为进一步的发展踩下刹车。

paragraphs.text: Many tech enthusiasts are still rallying around the promise of AI tools to create detailed images cheaply and quickly—anonymous tech supporters have already published a response to Butterick and Joseph Saveri's lawsuit on a website, using the "fair use" clause as the basis for why copyrighted images could be used by the tool.
paragraphs.translation: 许多科技爱好者仍在拥护 AI 工具廉价而快速地生成精细图像的前景——一些匿名的科技支持者已经在某网站上发布了对 Butterick 和 Joseph Saveri 诉讼的回应，以'合理使用'条款作为该工具能够使用受版权保护图像的依据。

paragraphs.text: Fair use, a legal doctrine that allows for a limited usage of copyrighted materials without permission by the original creators for purposes such as teaching and news sharing, is what a lot of generative model creators claim that their training data is covered by. However, since fair use applies differently to each case, it's hard to make a blanket statement about all works in a dataset as being applicable.
paragraphs.translation: '合理使用'是一项法律原则，允许在未经原创作者许可的情况下，出于教学、新闻分享等目的对受版权保护的材料进行有限度的使用；许多生成式模型的开发者声称，他们的训练数据正受该原则保护。然而，由于'合理使用'在每个案件中的适用情况各不相同，很难笼统地断言一个数据集中的所有作品都适用这一原则。

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: Why have three artists brought a lawsuit against Stability AI, DeviantArt, and Midjourney?

options.label: A
options.text: They claim that the use of the Stable Diffusion tool is a violation of law.

options.label: B
options.text: They claim these companies infringed their intellectual property rights.

options.label: C
options.text: They want to stop the use of all AI tools in the creation of art works.

options.label: D
options.text: They want to prevent artists from being compelled to rely on AI tools.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。首段与第二段指出艺术家起诉是因为这些 AI 工具'infringed the rights of thousands of artists'，且在数十亿张受版权保护的图像上训练'without compensation or consent'，即侵犯了艺术家的知识产权，与 B 一致。
questions.keySentence: alleging that the text-to-image AI tools have infringed the rights of thousands of artists

wrongOptions.A: 诉讼核心是侵犯知识产权，而非泛泛地指控'使用该工具违法'。
wrongOptions.C: 艺术家反对的是未经许可的版权使用，并非要求停止所有 AI 工具用于艺术创作。
wrongOptions.D: 文中未提及'阻止艺术家被迫依赖 AI 工具'。

questions.questionText: What will happen if Stable Diffusion and similar products are allowed to continue to operate as they do now, according to the law firm?

options.label: A
options.text: Intellectual property laws will be hard to enforce.

options.label: B
options.text: Fewer artists will invest talent in artistic creation.

options.label: C
options.text: Artists will lose their means of subsistence.

options.label: D
options.text: Copied works will flood the art market.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第四段律所指出可预见结果是这些产品'will replace the very artists'，并'eliminate "artist" as a viable career path'（让“艺术家”这一职业道路消失），即艺术家将失去谋生手段，与 C 一致。
questions.keySentence: they will eliminate 'artist' as a viable career path

wrongOptions.A: 文中未说知识产权法将难以执行。
wrongOptions.B: 'artist 这一职业消失'不等于'更少艺术家投入才华'，属偷换概念。
wrongOptions.D: '仿制作品充斥艺术市场'为无中生有。

questions.questionText: What makes artists furious aside from copyright infringement?

options.label: A
options.text: Art works produced with AI tools are not banned from art-sharing platforms.

options.label: B
options.text: Text-to-image generators have won such great popularity in the past year.

options.label: C
options.text: Their distorted signatures appear more and more frequently in AI art.

options.label: D
options.text: AI tools can bypass the considerable labor involved in creating art works.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第六段指出艺术家除对版权侵犯愤怒外，还'frustrated by how AI tools are able to sidestep the labor and art processes'（AI 工具能绕过他们必须经历的劳动与创作过程），与 D 一致。
questions.keySentence: they have also been frustrated by how AI tools are able to sidestep the labor and art processes they are required to go through

wrongOptions.A: 艺术家想封禁 AI 艺术是其行动，并非令其愤怒的额外原因。
wrongOptions.B: 工具流行是背景，非艺术家愤怒的原因本身。
wrongOptions.C: 扭曲签名是艺术家反对 AI 的原因之一，但题目问的是'除版权侵犯外'的原因，且原文强调的是绕过劳动过程。

questions.questionText: What do we learn from the passage about many AI enthusiasts?

options.label: A
options.text: They look forward to AI tools creating good-quality art works.

options.label: B
options.text: They claim artists can use copyrighted materials just as teachers do.

options.label: C
options.text: They support AI's limited use of copyrighted images without permission.

options.label: D
options.text: They wish the "fair use" clause would be applicable to all works in a dataset.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第八段指出科技爱好者以'fair use'条款为依据，认为该工具可使用受版权保护的图像；而'合理使用'允许在未经许可下对版权材料进行有限度使用，即他们支持 AI 未经许可地有限度使用版权图像，与 C 一致。
questions.keySentence: using the "fair use" clause as the basis for why copyrighted images could be used by the tool

wrongOptions.A: '期待生成高质量作品'非本段所述爱好者的核心主张。
wrongOptions.B: 把'合理使用'的教学等用途曲解为'艺术家可像教师那样使用版权材料'，偷换主体。
wrongOptions.D: 末段明确指出'合理使用'难以对数据集中所有作品一概适用，与该选项相反。

questions.questionText: What does the author think of the "fair use" clause in copyright law?

options.label: A
options.text: It may determine the final verdict of the case.

options.label: B
options.text: It may not apply to the present legal case.

options.label: C
options.text: It does not cover the works of all artists.

options.label: D
options.text: It is subject to different interpretations.

questions.analysis: 观点态度题。末段指出'fair use applies differently to each case'，且'it's hard to make a blanket statement about all works in a dataset as being applicable'，暗示合理使用未必适用于本案这种整批数据的情形，与 B 一致。
questions.keySentence: since fair use applies differently to each case, it's hard to make a blanket statement about all works in a dataset as being applicable

wrongOptions.A: 文中未提及该条款会'决定案件最终判决'。
wrongOptions.C: '不涵盖所有艺术家的作品'与原文'对每个案件适用情况不同'不完全对应，且非作者强调重点。
wrongOptions.D: 作者强调的是逐案适用、难以一概适用，而非'该条款有不同解释'。

questionGroups.title: Passage 2

paragraphs.text: On a warm October morning, Daniel Agok woke up to another disappointing day at his school in Wanyjok, South Sudan. The classes he had planned teaching computer skills to aspiring young professionals were canceled, due to an unreliable diesel generator and the absence of a municipal power grid in his area. Now, he would be losing frustrated customers as well as income. Agok is just one of the hundreds of millions of people in sub-Saharan Africa, many of whom are business owners, who still do not have dependable electricity. This inequitable access to energy continues to put their livelihood and future at risk.
paragraphs.translation: 在十月一个温暖的清晨，Daniel Agok 在南苏丹 Wanyjok 的学校里迎来了又一个令人失望的日子。他原计划为有抱负的年轻职场人士开设的计算机技能课程被取消了，原因是柴油发电机不可靠，而他所在地区又没有市政电网。如今，他不仅要损失收入，还要失去那些沮丧的学员。Agok 只是撒哈拉以南非洲数亿人中的一员，其中许多人是企业主，却仍然用不上可靠的电力。这种不公平的能源获取状况持续让他们的生计和未来面临风险。

paragraphs.text: The current system keeps a lid on the economic talents of people like Agok and his students. We must instead unleash their abilities and let Africa reach its true economic potential. That means wiring Africa with clean, dependable energy.
paragraphs.translation: 当前的体系压制了像 Agok 和他的学员这样的人的经济才能。相反，我们必须释放他们的能力，让非洲实现其真正的经济潜力。这意味着要用清洁、可靠的能源为非洲铺设电力网络。

paragraphs.text: Historically, national governments on the continent have led electrification efforts, but fewer than half of the people surveyed say that the national grid is providing a reliable supply of electricity.
paragraphs.translation: 从历史上看，非洲大陆的各国政府一直主导着电气化进程，但在接受调查的人中，只有不到一半的人表示国家电网能提供可靠的电力供应。

paragraphs.text: This has led to expensive and harmful temporary "solutions". In Nigeria alone, experts estimate people spend $13 billion every year on fuel for toxic, polluting generators. That number will only grow as the continent's population hits 2.5 billion people by 2050. Deploying modern grid infrastructure with speed and at scale is essential to replacing these temporary solutions with reliable and affordable alternatives.
paragraphs.translation: 这导致了昂贵且有害的临时'解决方案'。仅在尼日利亚，专家估计人们每年就要花费130亿美元为有毒、造成污染的发电机购买燃料。随着非洲大陆人口在2050年达到25亿，这个数字只会不断增长。以速度和规模部署现代电网基础设施，对于用可靠、可负担的替代方案取代这些临时办法至关重要。

paragraphs.text: The rapidly growing private power sector in Africa holds the key to achieving the speed and scale necessary to close the continent's energy access gap. Private companies today are building world-class infrastructure and driving forward economic growth with sustainable business models. In fact, many governments agree and have begun to embrace the private sector as partners in providing reliable power at scale. In South Africa, President Cyril Ramaphosa has streamlined licensing requirements and enlisted the private sector to play a key role.
paragraphs.translation: 非洲迅速增长的私营电力部门是实现填补非洲大陆能源获取缺口所需速度与规模的关键。如今，私营企业正在建设世界一流的基础设施，并以可持续的商业模式推动经济增长。事实上，许多政府对此表示认同，并已开始把私营部门作为大规模提供可靠电力的合作伙伴。在南非，Cyril Ramaphosa 总统简化了牌照审批要求，并让私营部门发挥关键作用。

paragraphs.text: South Africa is just one example. Across the continent, the private sector has delivered power faster and more reliably, and governments are increasingly turning to private partners.
paragraphs.translation: 南非只是一个例子。在整个非洲大陆，私营部门都以更快、更可靠的方式提供了电力，各国政府也越来越多地转向私营合作伙伴。

paragraphs.text: With the right funding and structure in place, the private sector will come together to provide this essential service. After all, electrifying sub-Saharan Africa is a $350 billion opportunity.
paragraphs.translation: 只要有合适的资金和架构到位，私营部门就会携手提供这项必不可少的服务。毕竟，为撒哈拉以南非洲通电是一个价值3500亿美元的商机。

paragraphs.text: Today, Daniel Agok is steadily growing his business in South Sudan. His town of Wanyjok was electrified by a private company, providing clean, reliable, and affordable power to his business and his neighbors. Agok now operates his growing computer skills training business smoothly. His classes are no longer affected by the smell and the constant noise of the diesel generator, and he saves money with more affordable power. His students are developing hardware and software skills.
paragraphs.translation: 如今，Daniel Agok 在南苏丹的生意正稳步壮大。他所在的 Wanyjok 镇由一家私营公司通电，为他的生意和邻居们提供清洁、可靠且可负担的电力。Agok 如今顺利经营着他日益壮大的计算机技能培训业务。他的课程不再受到柴油发电机气味和持续噪音的影响，而更实惠的电力也帮他省了钱。他的学员们正在发展硬件和软件技能。

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: What do we learn about the current electric supply system in Africa?

options.label: A
options.text: It curbs the economic development of the continent.

options.label: B
options.text: It mainly depends on the polluting diesel generators.

options.label: C
options.text: It is the primary cause of inequitable distribution of wealth.

options.label: D
options.text: It deprives many Africans of the opportunity to use computers.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第二段指出'The current system keeps a lid on the economic talents of people like Agok'，且首段称不公平的能源获取'put their livelihood and future at risk'，即现行供电体系抑制了非洲的经济发展，与 A 一致。
questions.keySentence: The current system keeps a lid on the economic talents of people like Agok and his students.

wrongOptions.B: 污染性柴油发电机是临时'解决方案'，非现行供电体系本身的主要依托。
wrongOptions.C: 文中未称其为财富分配不公的'首要原因'。
wrongOptions.D: 无法上计算机课只是 Agok 个例，非对整个体系的概括。

questions.questionText: What do we learn from the passage about Africa's past electrification efforts?

options.label: A
options.text: They have failed to meet most Africans' need of a reliable power supply.

options.label: B
options.text: They have failed to build a national grid to provide electric power.

options.label: C
options.text: They have unleashed the true economic potential of the continent.

options.label: D
options.text: They have aimed at wiring Africa with clean, dependable energy.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第三段指出各国政府主导电气化，但'fewer than half of the people surveyed say that the national grid is providing a reliable supply of electricity'，即过去的努力未能为多数非洲人提供可靠电力，与 A 一致。
questions.keySentence: fewer than half of the people surveyed say that the national grid is providing a reliable supply of electricity

wrongOptions.B: 原文是国家电网未能可靠供电，而非'未能建成国家电网'。
wrongOptions.C: '释放大陆真正经济潜力'是文中呼吁的目标，而非过去努力已达成的结果。
wrongOptions.D: '用清洁、可靠能源为非洲通电'是作者主张的方向，非对过去努力目标的描述。

questions.questionText: What is essential to tackling the power supply shortage in Africa?

options.label: A
options.text: Replacing temporary solutions with long-term strategies.

options.label: B
options.text: Accelerating economic growth with sustainable policies.

options.label: C
options.text: Restructuring national power generation companies.

options.label: D
options.text: Putting in place a large-scale modern power grid speedily.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第四段指出'Deploying modern grid infrastructure with speed and at scale is essential'，即快速、大规模地部署现代电网基础设施是关键，与 D 一致。
questions.keySentence: Deploying modern grid infrastructure with speed and at scale is essential to replacing these temporary solutions

wrongOptions.A: 原文强调用可靠可负担的替代方案取代临时办法，'长期策略'并非其关键表述。
wrongOptions.B: '以可持续政策加速经济增长'非本题所问的核心手段。
wrongOptions.C: 文中未提及'重组国家发电公司'。

questions.questionText: What are many governments in Africa doing to solve the electricity supply problem?

options.label: A
options.text: Focusing on building world-class infrastructures.

options.label: B
options.text: Relying on the private sector for scale economy.

options.label: C
options.text: Launching sustainable business models.

options.label: D
options.text: Cooperating with private companies.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第五、六段指出许多政府'have begun to embrace the private sector as partners'，且'governments are increasingly turning to private partners'，即与私营企业合作，与 D 一致。
questions.keySentence: many governments agree and have begun to embrace the private sector as partners in providing reliable power at scale

wrongOptions.A: 建设世界一流基础设施是私营企业所为，非政府的做法。
wrongOptions.B: '依赖私营部门实现规模经济'表述不准，原文是把私营部门作为合作伙伴。
wrongOptions.C: 以可持续商业模式推动增长的是私营企业，非政府。

questions.questionText: Why will private companies be motivated to join the effort of electrifying sub-Saharan Africa?

options.label: A
options.text: There is big money to be made.

options.label: B
options.text: They have enough funding in place.

options.label: C
options.text: South Africa has set a successful example.

options.label: D
options.text: Governments are turning to them for help.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第七段指出'electrifying sub-Saharan Africa is a $350 billion opportunity'（为撒哈拉以南非洲通电是一个价值3500亿美元的商机），即有巨额利润可赚，是私营企业的动力所在，与 A 一致。
questions.keySentence: electrifying sub-Saharan Africa is a $350 billion opportunity

wrongOptions.B: 原文说'只要有合适的资金到位'，是条件而非既有事实，不构成动机。
wrongOptions.C: 南非是私营部门成功供电的例子，非私营企业参与的动机。
wrongOptions.D: 政府转向私营部门是政府一方的行为，非私营企业自身的动机。

questionGroups.sourceText: 近年来，中国无人机（drone）产业蓬勃发展，出口量跃升为全球第一。中国的无人机以出色的稳定性、高清（high-definition）拍摄能力和便捷的操作，受到全球消费者的喜爱，在民用领域得到广泛应用。无人机已被国家纳入战略性新兴产业，逐步成为能满足多种场景需求的智能助手。在农村，无人机可精准识别农作物病虫害，高效喷洒农药。在城市，无人机可快速运送生鲜食品。在不久的将来，无人机能够在更多领域实现其独特价值，为经济社会发展注入新动能。

answer.modelTranslation: In recent years, China's drone industry has flourished, with its export volume leaping to first in the world. Thanks to their excellent stability, high-definition photography capabilities and convenient operation, Chinese drones are favored by consumers around the globe and have been widely applied in civilian fields. Drones have been included by the state in the category of strategic emerging industries and are gradually becoming intelligent assistants capable of meeting the needs of a variety of scenarios. In rural areas, drones can accurately identify crop diseases and pests and spray pesticides efficiently. In cities, drones can swiftly deliver fresh food. In the near future, drones will be able to realize their unique value in more fields, injecting new momentum into economic and social development.
translationNotes: '蓬勃发展'可译为 has flourished / has developed vigorously；'出口量跃升为全球第一'用 with its export volume leaping to first in the world 的独立主格结构衔接更自然
'以出色的稳定性……受到……喜爱'用 Thanks to ... 引导原因状语，主句 are favored by，避免头重脚轻
'高清拍摄能力'译为 high-definition photography capabilities，注意 high-definition 连字符
'纳入战略性新兴产业'译为 included in the category of strategic emerging industries
'病虫害'译为 diseases and pests；'喷洒农药'译为 spray pesticides
'为……注入新动能'译为 injecting new momentum into ...，用现在分词作伴随状语
scoringPoints: '无人机产业蓬勃发展，出口量跃升为全球第一'的句式衔接
'以出色的稳定性……受到全球消费者喜爱'的原因状语与被动语态
'纳入战略性新兴产业'的被动表达
'精准识别农作物病虫害，高效喷洒农药'的动词并列
'快速运送生鲜食品'的地道表达 swiftly deliver fresh food
'为经济社会发展注入新动能'的分词状语处理
整体时态（现在完成时+一般将来时）与逻辑连贯
